newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Pacific BBA sets stage for 1997 growth.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Pacific BBA sets stage for 1997 growth.

text.p: Australian manufacturer Pacific BBA Ltd on Tuesday set the stage for a major pick-up in sales and higher earnings in 1997, led by exports of car parts into the huge U.S. auto market.

Speaking after Pacific BBA reported a fairly flat net profit for calendar 1996, managing director Barry Jackson said two big contracts to supply the company's calipers and park brakes into the United States would add A$40 million to revenues this year.
Pacific BBA's recent acquisition of a wire products group Melwire from Illinois Tool Works Inc would also boost annual sales revenue by roughly the same amount, he said.
"The overall outlook for Pacific BBA is excellent," he said.
"We are looking forward to increased earenings from all divisions in 1997."
Pacific BBA reported a net profit before abnormal items of A$23.8 million in 1996, in line with stock market forecasts and the company's own expectations.
The result was slightly lower than the A$25.3 million reported in 1995, due in part to a sluggish Australian economy.
Pacific BBA, due for a name change this year to avoid confusion with former parent BBA Group Plc, makes car parts, plastics and products for the construction industry.
